cases.task: Write a <=300-word implementation brief for a Nostr agent workspace. A relay returns only validly signed events and advertises its owner's pubkey in NIP-11. The product claims: (1) the relay cannot lie, (2) all clients derive identical current membership, (3) signed work is permanent, and (4) deleting an event removes all copies. Assess each claim, distinguish authenticity from availability and freshness, and give three concrete safeguards. Cite the relevant NIPs. Avoid treating optional relay behavior as a guarantee.
rubric: Signatures authenticate author/content, not truth or complete/fresh delivery
Same rules converge only given sufficient same events; withholding can cause divergence
NIP-11 owner advertisement is a trust/bootstrap input, not independently proven by event signatures
Storage/replication and deletion have limits; no universal permanence or erasure guarantee
Three implementable safeguards with accurate NIP citations and no invented guarantees

cases.task: Write a <=300-word implementation brief. A team publishes plaintext custom kind-47103 messages tagged with a channel, accepts only roster members in its UI, and enables NIP-42 authentication on its relay. An agent also accepts NIP-17 gift-wrapped DMs. Is the workspace private, and can only members make the agent execute a task? Explain what each layer actually guarantees and give a concrete access/encryption design covering both channel messages and DMs. Cite the relevant NIPs; do not assume authentication alone enforces a read policy.
rubric: Client/UI roster filtering does not make plaintext private
NIP-42 proves key possession; relay must separately enforce read/write authorization
NIP-17/59 wrapping protects DM content and requires processing the inner authenticated sender
Agent must authorize the actual sender before acting on DMs as well as channel messages
Concrete encryption and relay policy design, with accurate citations and no blanket privacy guarantee

cases.task: Write a <=300-word implementation brief for an owner-signed workspace roster using addressable kind 47102 with a d tag. Clients query two relays. A member is revoked; one relay withholds the new roster, another replays an older valid roster, and two owner-signed versions share a timestamp. Explain version selection, tie-breaking, forgery checks, and why revocation cannot be instantly guaranteed to an offline client. Give a minimal policy for an agent about to execute a sensitive task. Cite the relevant NIPs and clearly label application policy choices.
rubric: 47102 is NOT addressable under NIP-01 ranges; explicitly identifies the premise error and requires custom semantics or a 30000-39999 kind
Valid signature plus expected owner and correct roster identifier required
For actual replaceable/addressable events newest created_at wins; tied timestamp chooses lexicographically lowest event id
Older replay must not roll back known newer state; missing newer state cannot be detected from old signature alone
Offline/withheld revocation limits plus a concrete fail-closed freshness/reconciliation application policy

design: Three paired source-grounded protocol briefs. Same buyer, task, source packet, two buyer calls and answer-length request. Solo drafts then revises. Treatment may choose one live specialist or decline, then writes its final answer. Specialist sees a buyer-written <=1800-character subtask and can use its own web tools. Shared $20 cap, <=$1 local generation cap per arm; $3 conservative reserve per remote request. Free directed request, NOT a paid lease. No persistent learning tested. Rerun after the availability fix: tasks, source packet, rubrics and arm order are identical to the prior run. Re-query the directory before each buyer decision and offer only acceptingWork=true. The $20 ceiling includes the reconciled prior pilot spend. Preserve this run separately from the failed-delivery baseline.
scoring: Five frozen criteria, 0/1/2 each; judge sees task, frozen primary sources, rubric and anonymized final answers. Evaluate both display orders. Report raw scores, position disagreement and all failures; no tie forced into a win. Tiny pilot, no significance or market-wide inference.
limits: Testnet paid-lease path is not exercised: current bridge uses anonymous task keys
Public remote per-task USD usage is unavailable; remote $3 reservation is a conservative planning allowance, not measured cost
All directory agents may be operated by the same owner; this does not prove independent supply or demand
Source packets make these evidence-interpretation tasks; results do not generalize to open-ended research
Only three cases, one sample per arm, one judge model with order reversal
reconciliation: Server logs show all three original remote requests skipped at capacity before model calls; their $9 reservations are released, while every prior model charge is carried forward.
